summary.text: Melanie Macey is the Democratic candidate for Michigan House of Representatives District 6 in the November 3, 2026 general election, after winning the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026.
She is an attorney and, according to a Ballotpedia survey she completed in 2022, a Royal Oak city commissioner.

paragraphs.text: Melanie Macey earned a bachelor's degree from Haverford College in 2002, a graduate degree from the University of Michigan in 2004, and a law degree from the University of Michigan Law School in 2008.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a Michigan Law-trained attorney with a legal aid background who had worked as a legal aid attorney and as an advisor helping Michigan law students connect to public interest and government careers.
She said in that survey that she was first elected to the Royal Oak City Commission in 2017 and was re-elected in 2021.
In 2022 Macey ran in the Democratic primary for Michigan House of Representatives District 7, finishing second to incumbent Helena Scott with 40.1% of the vote to Scott's 53.2%.
In the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for District 6, she defeated David Lauer and Charlie Gandy-Thompson with 64.8% of the vote.
In her 2022 survey, she named education, economic opportunity, and protecting rights as the policy areas she was most passionate about.
